thread.title: Sears Hometown And Outlet: The Slow Demise Of Sears Begins To Benefit Sears Hometown - Sears Hometown and Outlet Stores, Inc. (NASDAQ:SHOS)

author: Money Investor
title: Sears Hometown And Outlet: The Slow Demise Of Sears Begins To Benefit Sears Hometown - Sears Hometown and Outlet Stores, Inc. (NASDAQ:SHOS)
text:
Yes, the name Sears elicits venom from basically any investor or retail analyst and for a fairly good reason. To understand the update on Sears Hometown ( SHOS ), you have to understand the latest update on Sears Holdings ( SHLD ). The slow operational bankruptcy of Sears continues to play out on a daily basis. To Eddie Lampert's credit, he has proven 99% of the analysts and Seeking Alpha bears wrong. I will wager a $1 bet that there is not a single bearish author on this platform, who began calling for the company's demise as early as 2015, that proffered the argument that mid-way through 2018 the company would still be operating. Yet the company still stands, and with the recent news of Lampert himself readying to buy more assets from Sears, the slow unwind will continue. My bet is that Lampert buys Kenmore, part of the Home Services, and the Real Estate. Effectively everything that he has offered to buy. This will infuse significant cash into Sears Holdings, and I would wager another $1 that Sears is still in operations through all of 2019 at a minimum.
The update on Sears and more importantly, the update on key assets within Sears such as Kenmore has an impact on Sears Hometown. Sears Hometown is still, for better or worse (or in sickness and in health), largely married to Sears Holdings. SHOS received over 75% of its merchandise through supply agreements with Sears in FY 2017 . The "for worse" part of that equation is that Sears can't keep the stores stocked with tools and appliances and this has trickled down to SHOS. Management for SHOS noted that the step backward the company took in Q4 2017 was due in large part due to not having enough inventory in its stores. Sticking with the "for worse" theme, Sears has basically stopped advertising and supporting its key brands like Kenmore, Diehard, and Craftsman (which it now licenses). Sears is relying on its "members" to drive what remaining sales the company does get. SHOS took it on the chin in Q4 with Sears effectively being radio silent on the advertising front during holiday season when every other retailer was touting their deals.
On the "for better" side of the equation, it appears SHOS is finally in a position where they can begin the divorce proceedings. This will likely be that divorce where the parents stay together for a few more years, until the kids move out, but everyone knows the divorce is happening. SHOS is rapidly beginning to source inventory directly from manufacturers like Whirlpool (NYSE: WHR ) and bypassing the need to rely on Sears and whether or not they are paying their bills on time. SHOS also initiated their first nationwide advertising campaign in March of 2018. The advertising campaign is brilliant in its simplicity. In a short period of time, the company looked like it had climbed the hill, came tumbling back down, and has quietly started climbing it again while receiving zero coverage as to why. Here are the reasons why below.
SHOS Permanent Turnaround Has Begun SHOS gave us a false start in 2017 after reporting positive adjusted EBITDA in Q2 and Q3 of 2017. Q4 was pretty much a disaster after it appeared the company was on the verge of positive adjusted EBITDA for the full year. As noted earlier, lack of inventory and lack of Sears advertising and support hurt SHOS significantly in Q4 2017. Since that report, we have had a number of quiet but positive catalysts take place. When it appeared SHOS had turned the corner, the stock had moved up as high as $3.55 per share prior to the Q4 earnings release in late April. The share price was cut in half after that release falling to as low as $1.70. It quickly perked back up to $2.20 per share to end this past week, and I believe it could quickly move right back up to the $3.50 range over the next few weeks. There are not a lot of opportunities to make a 50% or more gain in a period of weeks, but this is one of them. Here are your forthcoming catalysts:
1) - The business has materially improved in Q1 2018. The company noted in their Q4 earnings release that the first 2 months of 2018 had seen YoY adjusted EBITDA improve by $6.0M to $6.5M compared to the prior year. In Q1 2017 , adjusted EBITDA was ($8.7M). On Friday, May 18th, the company held its annual meeting and gave an in-depth presentation and update on the business and strategic initiatives. The reason that shares spiked almost 15% on Friday was likely due to two sentences in a 60-page presentation ( see page 4 ). Those two sentences said that the company estimated adjusted EBITDA for Q1 2018 would show improvement of $10.5M to $11.5M compared to the prior year. Bear in mind that the quarter had already ended, and so the company likely knows the results and they should be at the high end of that range. We know that the first 2 months of Q1 saw $6.0M to $6.5M of improvement based on the Q4 earnings release from mid-April which covered results from February and March. Fast forward 30 days and that improvement jumped by another $4.0M to $5.0M. Effectively, the company saw a gigantic leap (relatively speaking) in April's performance. This coincided with a number of initiatives being in place such as having inventory (shocking that having something to sell helps your results), a national advertising campaign, and the company focusing on pricing initiatives in its Outlet business to drive significant margin improvement. I would highly suggest reading the entire presentation here .
2) - Branding and advertising - SHOS is threading the needle of using the Sears history, which still means something to many Americans, while emphasising how SHOS is different. The advertising campaign basically focuses on how everyday Americans own their SHOS business and play at the very real theme that most of us genuinely want to see small businesses succeed. Wherever you live, there is a mom and pop shop or restaurant, that certainly is not the cheapest option, but they provide something different. It might be the goods or might be the service or it simply might be the relationship you have with the store owner. A wide swath of consumers still wants to have personal interaction when they are purchasing something and to know that if something goes wrong, they can talk to the CEO of the company and get an answer. The store owners are the CEO in effect, and SHOS is playing to the personal side of what many consumers value. Trusted brands and product but more importantly, trusted relationships. If you don't believe me, watch an advertisement here for yourself. This particular advertisement has been viewed over 4M times in the last month since it landed on YouTube. That is an insane amount of views for a SHOS commercial. Search any of your favorite brands and you will be hard-pressed to find a commercial on YouTube go viral to the extent this one did. Kudos to the SHOS market team on this campaign.
3) - Earnings in June - SHOS was delayed in reporting its Q4 2017 earnings and used the time allowed given their SEC status and size which gives incremental time for 10-K reporting. They typically report Q1 earnings the first week of June. They have a maximum of 45 days from May 2nd (qtr. end) to report earnings. I would expect to see them back on track with an early June reporting date. We know that the earnings will look great. Adjusted EBITDA will be positive considering we know it was ($8.7M) in Q1 2017 and were just told at the annual meeting that it would be up between $10.5M and $11.5M YoY. We saw the stock go down 50% on a bad earnings report. I would not expect to see it head back to $3.50 per share on a positive earnings report.
4) - 2018 Outlook - The company is likely going to start the year with $2-3M of positive adjusted EBITDA. Q2 2017 and Q3 2017 were positive adjusted EBITDA quarters the prior year. If the market comes around to seeing a path for SHOS to begin generating positive adjusted EBITDA again, I would just tell everyone to buckle up for the ride. This is a company with a $50M market cap and that could potentially report $10-20M of adjusted EBITDA in 2018 by just replicating the performance from the prior year in Q2 and Q3 and then not repeating the mistake made in Q4.
5) - Short Interest - Over 3M shares sold short. Likely something close to 50% of the effective float is sold short. This is a stock that trades 100-200K shares a day on a good day. It will be a very crowded trade if shorts head for the exit.
6) - Sears Holdings Earnings - Sears is not going bankrupt yet. We will find that out again likely this week or in the last few days of May. This will remind the shorts and everyone else that the black swan risk for SHOS involving an abrupt shut down of Sears Holdings is just not going to happen.
7) - IT Transformation - SHOS has spent $60M in cold hard cash over the last 3 years developing an IT system to not be reliant on Sears Holdings. That black hole of cash usage is coming to an end providing two key catalysts. Think about what SHOS could do when they are not dumping $60M of cash into building IT systems (hint: eventually paying down debt and buying back shares or distributing it to shareholders). More importantly, the company can provide a modern day technology experience for customers and source inventory from vendors directly without needing Sears.
8) - Sears Store Closings - SHOS is not allowed to operate in MSAs where Sears Holdings has an open store. As Sears stores close, SHOS will continue to have a chance to open shop in areas that over time have been successful for Sears and represent easy opportunities to capture growth. SHOS is also able to serve those areas via its e-commerce platform when a Sears store closes. This will be a meaningful tailwind for years to come.
The Risk Is Minimal And The Opportunity Is Enormous Let's recap. SHOS is a $50M market cap company. It generates $1.5B of revenue on an annual basis. It has $135M of working capital with no liquidity concerns. The company has an actual plan in place to succeed as stand-alone business as evidenced by spending $60M on IT systems over the last 3 years. The company saw accelerating improvement across its business over the last 12 weeks, and we are about to get an earnings report telling us (but you heard it here first).
Could things go wrong? Absolutely. Could the advertising be a short-term lift that is unsustainable? Sure. Have I been wrong on the call for a turnaround in this name before? Yes sir, indeed I have. But I know that Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) might go up 10%, Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ) maybe 20%, and lots of other really cool companies are sexy investments but they are not doing to go up 50% in 30 days. SHOS very well might. The reality is that this is a company that could figure out a way back to earning 5% pre-tax income over time on $1-1.5B in sales. Even if the company shrinks, its store count and revenues fall to $1B, a 5% operating margin will be $50M in pre-tax. You slap a 5x multiple on that business and it is worth $250M. That is a 5 bagger ladies and gentlemen. It is not hard to believe and it sure sounds better than a 2% yield and betting on Apple going up 10% more to become a trillion dollar company.
I am ready for the rocket to lift off. Hope you are there with me in early June when it happens!
Disclosure: I am/we are long SHOS.
